name: Tirhakah
overview: Tirhakah was a male king known specifically as the King of Cush, a region historically associated with Ethiopia. His role is noted in the Bible, particularly in 2 Kings 19:9, where he is identified by this unique royal title. There is no additional information regarding his tribe or personal background in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Tirhakah appears as a proper name in the biblical text without a provided meaning. He is also referred to by the title 'King of Cush,' which designates his rulership over the land of Cush, commonly linked to Ethiopia. Both the name and title are found in 2 Kings 19:9.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Tirhakah beyond his identification as King of Cush. There are no noted relatives or tribal affiliations mentioned in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Tirhakah's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his position as the King of Cush during a critical historical period. His mention in 2 Kings 19:9 situates him within the geopolitical landscape affecting Israel and Judah, highlighting the broader context of foreign powers interacting with God's people.
